sourceState: Committed M4.6 application-byte threshold re-evaluation; package outputs were rebuilt and scanned before this decision was recorded

protocol.measure: sum of emitted local graph artifact filesystem bytes; direct external imports and nonliteral loads recorded separately
protocol.repetitions: one deterministic post-build artifact scan; this is a graph inventory, not a noisy runtime timing measurement

theme.scope: Compatibility runtime entrypoint: full theme provider, selectors, token-theme scopes, dependency plans, recipes, structured style resolution and legacy token compatibility.

theme-core.scope: Lean runtime entrypoint: common provider, hooks and token/style resolution needed by the ordinary application path, excluding compatibility-only advanced exports.

tokens.scope: Ordinary runtime-safe token contract and theme entrypoint: domain definitions, contract construction, token identities, aliases and theme snapshots. Effect remains in explicit schema/optic subpaths.

splitBudget.policy: Record current graph sizes as candidate baselines; require explicit reviewer approval for absolute ceilings and allowed growth before adding metrics to budgets.json.

reason: The retained 11,307-byte selector measures the old compatibility theme graph, while the current public runtime has materially expanded functionality and separate theme-core and tokens entrypoints.

Reducing the current compatibility graph to the historical size would require removing supported behavior or changing the API contract; the evidence does not identify an equivalent same-functionality reduction target.
The current graphs are deterministic and independently inspectable, so they provide suitable candidate baselines for split budgets without pretending that a reviewer has approved the policy.
The existing budget registry remains the source of qualification truth and stays unchanged and fail-closed until concrete split ceilings are approved.

admissionRequirements: Review the three candidate entrypoint scopes and decide whether ESM and CJS share one budget or have format-specific ceilings.
Approve an absolute maximum and allowed-growth rule for each admitted graph, with a reviewer and dated evidence record.
Add selectors and baseline evidence to packages/css/bench/budgets.json only after the split policy is approved.
Keep application bundle, Hermes bytecode, startup, frame, allocation and retained-memory metrics separate from emitted graph bytes.
Obtain the outstanding release-Hermes device evidence before activating the whole performance registry; Android remains parked until the final device-enabled move.
limits: Graph bytes are emitted JavaScript artifact sizes, not minified/Hermes contribution or native startup/frame/allocation/retained-memory performance.
The token graph is intentionally larger than its 1,029/1,529-byte entry file because its four local chunks are part of the emitted graph.
No package dependency, public API, native target or Android qualification state changed in this decision slice.
